raw_response:
I will keep this year simple and steady. I have farmed a long time, and with some family labor working off-farm, I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too labor-heavy. I will put the biggest area into cotton because that is my main crop and the one I trust most on my land. I will keep wheat and maize in moderate areas so I have grain and cash flow, and I will keep stevia on a smaller area because it can pay well but needs closer care. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water to protect yield at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. I will use better seed where it helps me most, keep fertilizer at a medium level that matches my experience, and avoid excessive pesticide spraying unless the field really needs it. I will plough the crops where I want a cleaner seedbed and better rooting, and I will use rotary tillage where faster preparation is enough. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield. I will aim for stable production, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole 64 mu.
